title: Acceptance Hallmark: Dedicated Capacity Hallmark Harness & Benchmark Manifest
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define and deliver a reproducible benchmarking and customer-acceptance manifest for Dedicated capacity that validates throughput guarantees, autoscaler safety, and fleet controls. Deliverables: a lightweight, opinionated harness (HallmarkRunner) for replaying tenant-mix traffic; a benchmark methodology document with fidelity tiers; an acceptance test checklist and runbook for customer signoff; telemetry and artifact templates for evidence submissions. The goal is a repeatable artifact bundle customers and solutions engineers can use to certify Dedicated pools for contractual SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: HallmarkRunner can execute end-to-end runs that include: smoke, ramp, sustain (10m+), microburst, and graceful teardown
Sustained throughput documented: runs produce reproducible QPS within ±5% across three independent runs for the same config
Tail latency SLOs: p95 and p99 measured against target profiles with artifacts in TelemetryLedger dashboard
Autoscaler correctness: scale-up and scale-down events observed and annotated; no thrash (back-to-back scale events within cooldown window) during sustained and burst phases
Failure modes exercised: OOM/evictions, kernel fallback, model-variant fallback; runbook contains mitigation steps and RCA template
Customer acceptance packet contains: run report PDF, raw telemetry bundle, run configuration (seeded), and a signed signoff checklist
No production changes required to run harness on Dedicated (only config flags and test workload injection).
test_plan: Stage 1: Local sanity — run HallmarkRunner on dev cluster with synthetic 1-tenant load; validate telemetry ingestion (10m)
Stage 2: Controlled replay — Replay a 24-hour tenant slice at 5x real QPS in staging to exercise autoscaler policies
Stage 3: Fidelity tier runs — Tier A (microburst-heavy, short bursts), Tier B (steady QPS, long sustain), Tier C (mixed realistic tenant-mix) — each run repeated 3 times
Stage 4: Customer Acceptance — run Tier C with customer-provided traces (or tenant-mix template) and capture signoff artifacts
Stage 5: Regression — nightly smoke run with reduced config to validate no regressions to batching and KV cache hit rate
telemetry_and_metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency for generation and routing steps
Token/sec and tokens per request distribution
GPU utilization and GPU memory headroom per node
Batching efficiency: avg batch size, batch latency contribution
KV cache hit rate and cache eviction counts
Autoscaler events: timestamped scale decisions, target size, cooldown windows
Error rates: 5xx, timeouts, throttles, model-variant fallbacks
Fairness: per-tenant throughput deviation and latency skew
